newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Difficult to proceed with Iraq oil deal-UK envoy.
newsitem.headline: Difficult to proceed with Iraq oil deal-UK envoy.

text.p: Britain's deputy ambassador to the United Nations, Stephen Gomersall, said Friday that implementation of Iraq's oil-for-food deal currently was "very difficult" in the wake of last weekend's military attack by Baghdad on protected Kurdish zones in the north of the country.

"We have discussed that (the oil-for-food resolution) actively during the week. It is the (U.N.) secretary-general's decision as to when circumstances will permit that resolution to be implemented on the ground but clearly the events of a week ago make it very difficult for him to go ahead at this point," Gomersall said.
Gomersall reiterated Britain's position that it does not want the deal stalled indefinitely, but couldn't say when the implementation might proceed.

"It is the wish of the council as a whole and of Britain, as one of the countries that sponsored resolution 986 (the oil-for-food), that it should go ahead for the humanitarian purpose for which it serves as soon as circumstances permit," Gomersall said.

Following Baghdad's incursions last weekend, United Nations secretary-general Boutros Boutros-Ghali suspended implementation of the deal, which allows Iraq to sell up to $2 billion of oil to pay for badly needed food and medicine for ordinary Iraqis.
Iraq has not been allowed to export oil since sanctions were imposed in the wake of its 1990 invasion of Kuwait.

The United Nations has said it suspended implentation of the deal, which was expected to see Iraqi oil start flowing again in September, because of worries about the safety of its staff in Iraq who are charged with monitoring equitable distribution of goods and to make sure Baghdad doesn't cheat on the strict rules under which it is allowed.
The U.N. hasn't said how long implementation is likely to be delayed since last week's suspension.
